purpose: Register a representative set of Human Infra domains as Q2/L2 model-candidate-variable bridge rows. Each row states where the domain could enter a future life-path model while keeping coefficients, causal effects, calibrated prediction, medical advice, intervention ranking and individual death-date outputs blocked.

currentDecision.reason: The register maps domains to candidate model positions only. It does not supply parameters, causal estimates, cohort calibration, clinical validity or individual-use authority.

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Changes the time-cost boundary for waiting on future external technology windows.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate channel for effective time, subjective time and external reference-time differentials.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: If a future waiting path changes subject-experienced time relative to external technological time, it may change the cost of reaching later technology states.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: scenario-defined waiting multiplier, exit condition, continuity condition and opportunity-cost record
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: effective time, future option value and continuity-preserving waiting cost
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: physical feasibility, exit probability, continuity preservation and tail risk
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to B0 if the scenario lacks exit, continuity, governance or bounded time-accounting definitions.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No engineering feasibility claim, no survival prediction, no individual advice and no claim that time differential alone creates net benefit.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: scenario card with metric, orbit/waiting path, exit, continuity, risk and opportunity-cost fields

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Reframes terminal biological failure as a possible suspended-state and future-recovery boundary problem.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate option-value and continuity-boundary row, not a resurrection or survival estimate.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: If biostasis preserves identity-relevant structure under bounded assumptions, it may preserve a future recovery option after ordinary biological continuity fails.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: preservation protocol class, structural preservation claims, revival evidence boundary and legal/consent status
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: post-terminal preservation discourse and future-recovery hypothesis space
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: future option value and subject-continuity boundary condition
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: revival feasibility, structural sufficiency, identity continuity and legal consent
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if a claim implies revival, immortality or medical effectiveness without external evidence.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No revival probability, no clinical recommendation, no legal advice and no individual decision support.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: bounded source cards separating preservation, damage, revival and identity-continuity claims

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Targets biological source-state maintenance by separating cellular age-state reset from identity loss.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate transition modifier for future tissue-function trajectories, not a human lifespan effect.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Partial reprogramming may affect cell identity stability, epigenetic age markers and tissue repair capacity, which could later enter state-transition hypotheses.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: cell identity markers, epigenetic clocks, tissue-function assays, tumor-risk and delivery-control evidence
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: preclinical, cell, tissue or tightly governed clinical disease contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: healthspan proxy, tissue function, repair capacity and safety boundary
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: dedifferentiation, tumor risk, delivery control, tissue specificity and human translation
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if biomarker rejuvenation is treated as human lifespan extension or if safety gates are missing.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No anti-aging treatment advice, no human lifespan estimate, no therapy ranking and no individual recommendation.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: source cards separating in vitro, animal, local-organ clinical and whole-body claims

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Controls a major catastrophic biological failure mode that can terminate subject continuity.
bridgeRows.variableFamily: cancer incidence / detection / treatment hazard channel
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate hazard-family row for future aggregate disease-risk modeling.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Cancer prevention, early detection and treatment continuity may shift disease onset, progression, survival and disability hazards.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: incidence, stage at detection, screening coverage, treatment access, survival and late-effect measures
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: mortality, disease-specific survival, healthspan and functional continuity
bridgeRows.causalStatus: mixed evidence class requiring design-specific separation
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: lead-time bias, overdiagnosis, treatment toxicity, competing risks and population transfer
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if screening, diagnosis, treatment or survival claims are merged without endpoint and bias separation.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No individual screening, diagnostic, treatment, prognosis, insurance or medical advice.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: endpoint-specific source cards and future target-trial or survival-analysis design notes

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Improves observation of biological state without directly proving intervention benefit.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate observation-process row for state measurement, stratification or validation planning.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Biomarkers and biological-age clocks may measure aspects of biological state or risk but require validation against functional endpoints and mortality outcomes.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: clock age, pace-of-aging measure, biomarker panel, validation cohort and endpoint alignment
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: biomarker validation and observational cohort contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: state measurement quality, healthspan proxy, risk stratification and validation diagnostics
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: surrogate endpoint validity, population transfer, assay drift and reverse causation
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if a clock improvement is equated with true lifespan extension or clinical benefit.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No individual biological-age interpretation, no treatment advice, no lifespan prediction and no intervention ranking.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: validation source cards linking biomarker, endpoint, population, uncertainty and reporting boundary

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Maintains immune defense, vaccine response and infection resilience as source-body continuity conditions.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate hazard and recovery row for infection, immune aging and response durability.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Immune repertoire diversity, immunosenescence and vaccine response may affect infection risk, recovery, hospitalization and mortality hazards.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: immune repertoire markers, vaccine response, infection incidence, hospitalization and immune-age indicators
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: aging, immunization and infection-risk research contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: infection resilience, mortality, hospitalization and recovery capacity
bridgeRows.causalStatus: mechanistic and observational; intervention-specific causal design required
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: variant exposure, prior infection, immune history, vaccine platform and population transfer
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if immune markers are promoted to generalized longevity effects without endpoint-specific evidence.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No vaccine, infection, immune-testing, medication or medical advice.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: source cards separating immune-marker associations, vaccine effectiveness and aging-specific endpoint claims

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Improves the subject's ability to choose, persist, inhibit distraction and execute long-horizon tasks.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate policy-quality row for adherence, task completion, risk avoidance and learning loops.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Attention and executive control may alter which actions are selected, sustained and corrected across time.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: attention measures, executive-function tasks, self-regulation proxies, task-completion and adherence signals
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: cognitive performance, work, learning and self-management contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: effective action density, adherence, learning, risk avoidance and future option value
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: measurement validity, context transfer, fatigue, stress and socioeconomic confounding
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if attention is treated as a direct lifespan variable rather than an action-policy mediator.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No diagnosis, medication, productivity prescription, employment decision or individual ranking.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: source cards linking executive-control measures to adherence, task completion and health behavior endpoints

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Converts calendar survival into usable effective time for action, learning, recovery and creation.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate time-accounting row separate from biological survival.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: The same survival duration can yield different effective-time budgets depending on waiting, administrative burden, care burden, sleep, work and task friction.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: time-use records, waiting time, administrative burden, care hours, sleep/recovery time and task-friction measures
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: time-use, service access, caregiving, work and daily-function contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: effective time, subjective time quality, opportunity cost and action density
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: self-report error, context transfer, hidden labor and distributional inequality
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if effective time is collapsed into lifespan or treated as universally comparable without measurement protocol.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No personal scheduling advice, employment ranking, productivity scoring or individual quality-of-life judgment.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: measurement protocol distinguishing calendar time, effective time, subjective time and care/admin burden

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Changes the external rate at which candidate interventions and biological tools become available.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate external technology-window row for future intervention arrival and adoption assumptions.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: AI-assisted design may affect discovery cost, candidate generation, experimental throughput and the probability that useful interventions become available within a time horizon.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: candidate generation rate, validation throughput, preclinical success, clinical translation and cost/time metrics
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: biomedical discovery pipelines and translational research infrastructure
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: technology-window probability, intervention availability and research-cycle acceleration
bridgeRows.causalStatus: technology-system mechanism, not human clinical effect
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: benchmark leakage, wet-lab validation gap, safety, regulatory translation and access inequality
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if discovery acceleration is treated as proven patient outcome or longevity effect.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No drug efficacy claim, no therapy selection, no investment advice and no patient prediction.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: source cards separating in silico design, wet-lab validation, clinical translation and access pathways

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Converts medical knowledge and services into reachable prevention, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate access gate for whether an intervention can be received, continued and escalated.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Healthcare access affects detection timing, treatment continuity, follow-up, medication availability and escalation before failure.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: coverage, distance, wait time, usual source of care, appointment availability, cost barriers and follow-up completion
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: health-service access, primary care, specialty care and care-continuity contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: adoption probability, delayed diagnosis, treatment continuity, morbidity and mortality risk
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: selection bias, local system variation, insurance design, quality differences and unmet need
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if access is treated as equivalent to effective treatment or individual outcome guarantee.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No provider recommendation, insurance advice, triage advice, diagnosis or medical decision support.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: data cards for access measures, care-continuity endpoints and population stratification

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Converts dispersed claims into reproducible evidence, reusable artifacts and model-governed knowledge.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate governance and uncertainty-control row for whether evidence can enter a model.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Research infrastructure affects replication, source traceability, data availability, preregistration, reporting quality and model admissibility.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: open data, preregistration, repository availability, reporting checklist, replication status and risk-of-bias assessment
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: research systems, open science and translational evidence pipelines
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: evidence certainty, model admission readiness, uncertainty reduction and translation speed
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: publication bias, reproducibility, reporting bias, data access and incentive distortion
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if source traceability, reporting standard or independent review is missing.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No claim that better research infrastructure itself proves intervention efficacy or model calibration.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: standards-to-gate mapping across TRIPOD, PROBAST, STROBE, RECORD, CONSORT, PRISMA and GRADE

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Maintains the resource buffer needed to access care, tools, stable environments and future options.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate enabling-resource gate for intervention adoption, persistence and risk recovery.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Financial resilience may affect affordability, time flexibility, housing stability, medical access, technology adoption and recovery from shocks.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: income stability, savings buffer, debt burden, insurance, out-of-pocket cost, benefit access and financial shock measures
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: household finance, health economics and social determinants contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: adoption probability, recovery probability, effective time, stress burden and future option value
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: reverse causation, wealth-health confounding, policy setting and measurement error
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if wealth is treated as a direct longevity intervention without causal design and distributional boundary.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No financial advice, eligibility advice, credit scoring, insurance advice or individual ranking.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: source cards separating affordability, access, shock recovery, stress and confounding pathways

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Captures environmental and community-level conditions that shape exposure, recovery, service access and resilience.
bridgeRows.variableFamily: community vulnerability / social determinants / exposure-context channel
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate contextual uncertainty and stratification row for population transfer and vulnerability gradients.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Community vulnerability may alter exposure, access, stress, environmental burden, disaster recovery and baseline risk.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: area deprivation, SVI-like indices, environmental exposure, service density, food/housing/transport access and local health estimates
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: community health, environmental justice and population vulnerability contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: applicability, transfer boundary, access probability, hazard heterogeneity and recovery capacity
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: ecological fallacy, area-to-individual transfer, measurement aggregation and policy confounding
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if area-level vulnerability is used as an individual trait or deterministic prediction.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No individual risk scoring, eligibility decision, policing, insurance use or stigmatizing ranking.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: source cards that separate area-level context, individual exposure, access pathway and transfer limits

bridgeRows.subjectContinuityFunction: Preserves mobility, strength, cardiometabolic function and daily task execution capacity.
bridgeRows.candidateModelRole: Candidate state and function row for healthspan, effective time and risk stratification.
bridgeRows.mechanismStatement: Physical activity and mobility may affect functional status, falls, cardiometabolic risk, independence and recovery capacity.
bridgeRows.measurementProxy: activity level, gait speed, grip strength, chair stand, balance, falls, ADL/IADL and cardiorespiratory fitness
bridgeRows.populationOrSetting: mobility, aging, rehabilitation and functional-health contexts
bridgeRows.endpointOrOutcomeFamily: functional status, healthspan, effective time, fall risk, morbidity and mortality
bridgeRows.causalStatus: mixed intervention/behavior evidence requiring population and safety boundaries
bridgeRows.uncertaintyChannel: reverse causation, baseline health, injury risk, adherence, measurement device and population transfer
bridgeRows.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if activity association is used as individual exercise prescription or direct lifespan effect.
bridgeRows.prohibitedUse: No exercise prescription, rehabilitation advice, injury-risk decision, medical advice or individual ranking.
bridgeRows.nextEvidenceNeeded: source cards linking mobility measures to function, mortality, falls and causal intervention designs
